blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Soaring fuel prices driven by the Middle East conflict pushed inflation in the Philippines to a 44-month high of 7.8 percent in October, the government said Thursday, as the country continues to struggle with a devalued peso. The latest inflation number was the highest since the 8.6 percent recorded in February 2023, chief Philippine statistician Dennis Mapa said, topping analysts’ forecast of 7.6 percent. “The main reason for the rise in inflation in October compared to September is the 20 percent rise in transport costs,” he told a news conference.
